correctness.rationale: At fixed vertex coordinate x, the conjugacy classes are exactly the cosets of the image of the displayed commutator map in R^E. For any lift x_v=c_vπ^a_v (including the zero coordinate represented by π^ℓ), the units c_v are removed by edge-row and vertex-column rescaling. Over the fraction field the remaining matrix is D_E B D_V^(-1), with scales π^(a_u+a_v) on edge rows and π^a_v on vertex columns. Cycle rows are dependent; forest rows give a nonzero square minor precisely on deleting one root column per edge-containing tree, with no extraneous columns. Leaf elimination gives determinant ±1 in the incidence matrix. The scaled determinant has valuation sum_v (d_F(v)-1)a_v over incident vertices plus the sum of omitted root valuations, minimized by a least-valuation root in each component. Thus the forest minima are precisely the Smith determinantal-divisor valuations. Reducing the Smith diagonal gives each nonzero image order q^max(ℓ-d_j,0) and is valid even if the lift of a zero coordinate is nonzero upstairs. Each x then contributes q^(ℓm-s) classes; the number of x with a given truncated valuation vector is (q-1)^b q^e. Expanding the resulting terms gives the asserted positivity, including with no edges, isolated vertices, or residue characteristic two. Independent commutator-image enumeration for P4 at level two gives class counts (64,64,208,192,352,128,64) at sizes 1 through 64 in powers of two both over Z/4 and over F2[t]/(t²); direct evaluation of the forest expression on its 81 valuation vectors gives the same vector and total 1072.

value.rationale: The exact class-size strata are natural invariants beyond the total count. The forest formula links them to computable graph data uniformly across residue fields and ramification, and its nonnegative summands settle the total positivity question across graphs and levels. The already known P4 total by itself would not supply value.
residual_risks: The enumeration need not be efficient and makes no claim about a compact rational zeta function or its poles.
